_note: ENGINE REGISTRY - which engine may be called, and for what. WHICH ENGINE DELIVERS IS DERIVED: it comes from config/delivery_profiles.json via scripts/pipeline.py, which rewrites `default`, `catalog_approved`, `allowed_for` and `blocked_for` in this file. Do not hand-edit those. Exactly one engine delivers at a time and every other engine is blocked from every delivered pixel - that invariant is asserted by scripts/engine.py --check in both states. Read this file; never hard-code engine ids, endpoints or tool names in scripts/.
auto_fallback_note: On ANY failure of the live engine (generation, timeout, API, connector, quality, geometry) the engine does NOT change. Retry inside the live engine. Changing engines is always a deliberate switch: python scripts/pipeline.py --use <profile>. docs/21 §1a.

higgsfield.catalog_block_reason: Delivery runs on 'openflow' while config/delivery_profiles.json active = 'gflow-nb2'. Switch with: python scripts/pipeline.py --use <profile>.

openflow.install: claude mcp add --transport http openflow https://openflowmcp.com/mcp
openflow.backend: Google Flow via unofficial bridge (Veo video; Nano Banana 2 / Pro / Lite images). Google publishes no API for Flow; this server drives a real Google account session.
requires: explicit --engine openflow on the command (never implicit, never a fallback)
MCP server installed and Google account connected by the user
openflow.security_note: Third-party hosted bridge. The user's Google password is entered on Google's own page, but the resulting session is exercised by openflowmcp.com. Do not connect an account the user has not explicitly chosen to expose.

auth.transport_auth: HTTP bearer header, stored in the user's ~/.claude.json (project scope). NEVER stored in this repo, never in .claude/settings.local.json, never printed.
auth.revoke_at: https://myaccount.google.com/device-activity - the grant appears as a DEVICE session, not as an app under 'Apps with access'.
auth.token_note: Onboarding used a single-use oauth2_4/ code from accounts.google.com/EmbeddedSetup, exchanged server-side for a Google master token. That master token lives on openflowmcp.com, not here.

capabilities_observed.images: available (free image quota 25, no hard limit reported)
capabilities_observed.video: NOT available - requires a paid subscription at https://openflowmcp.com/account
capabilities_observed.note: Engine 2 was added mainly for video, and video is exactly what the free tier withholds. Until a subscription exists, engine 2 can only do non-delivery image exploration - which it is already blocked from delivering.

let a non-delivering engine write into deliveries/ or workspace/golden/<SKU>/ render slots
selection_rules.authorization_phrase_to_change_productio: Superseded 2026-08-22: the switch is now an explicit command (scripts/pipeline.py --on/--off) run only on direct user instruction. No phrase is required; no automatic switch is permitted.

universal_policy._note: POLICY SUPREMACY (user 2026-08-21): project policy outranks every engine, mode, model and tool. Whatever generates the pixels, these rules still apply. This block does NOT restate the rules - each entry POINTS AT its single owner so there is one source of truth and nothing can drift. No engine record may declare an exemption; scripts/engine.py --check enforces that and attaches this block to every resolve().
universal_policy.applies_to: every engine in this file, present and future, and every generation mode (text-to-image, image-to-image, video, upscale, exploration)
universal_policy.on_conflict: If an engine cannot satisfy a blocking rule, the engine loses: do not relax the rule, do not deliver, report the limit and stop.
universal_policy.single_source_rule: One topic, one owner. A new rule must extend the EXISTING owner (superseding it on the same registry key), never open a second rule on a parallel key. policy/check.py STOPs on two active rules sharing a key and on a broken supersession chain.
